Claim 1 (Currently Amended): A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
__a hardware entropy source configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;__
__a function processor circuit configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;__
__a pseudorandom number generator circuit configured to be seeded with the second entropy value and to generate a random number; and__
__a cryptographic processor circuit configured to produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.__

Claim 2 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein __the cryptographic processor circuit is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number__.

Claim 3 (Currently Amended): The system __of__ claim 1, wherein __the cryptographic processor circuit is configured to__:
__implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and__
__produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key__.

Claim 4 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein __the hardware entropy source comprises__ a ring oscillator __configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values__.

Claim 5 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein __the hardware entropy source comprises__ a single hardware source __configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values__.

Claim 6 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein __the hardware entropy source comprises__ a plurality of independent hardware sources __configured to generate the plurality of independent first entropy values__.

Claim 7 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and __the function processor circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function__.

Claim 8 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 7, wherein __the function processor circuit is configured to__:
__divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;__
__apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and__
__concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value__.

Claim 9 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and __the function processor circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function__.

Claim 10 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and __the function processor circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer__.

Claim 11 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein __the function processor circuit is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value__.

Claim 12 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein __the function processor circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value__.

Claim 13 (Currently Amended): A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
__generating a plurality of independent first entropy values using a hardware entropy source;__
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

Claim 14 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

Claim 15 (Previously presented): The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least: implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

Claim 16 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein __generating the plurality of independent first entropy values includes generating the plurality of independent first entropy values using__ a ring oscillator __as the hardware entropy source__.

Claim 17 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein __the hardware entropy source comprises__ a single hardware source, and wherein __generating__ the plurality of independent first entropy values includes __generating__ the plurality of independent first entropy values __using the single hardware source__.

Claim 18 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein __the hardware entropy source comprises__ a plurality of independent hardware sources, and wherein __generating__ the plurality of independent first entropy values includes __generating__ the plurality of independent first entropy values __using the plurality of independent hardware sources__.

Claim 19 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

Claim 20 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 21 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

Claim 22 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

Claim 23 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

Claim 24 (Previously presented): The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
